source.label: Turan's exact local implication under the Lindelof hypothesis

reviewer: Claude Code reading of a published source; fresh medium reviewer

claims.summary: Published (Turan 1984, Theorem 36.1), under the Lindelof hypothesis: for 0 < delta < 1/4 (bound uncertain in the scan), 6 delta^2 log(3/delta) <= b <= 1, delta <= b/a <= 1/2, if |sum over N1 <= n <= N2 of Lambda(n) n^(-i tau0)| < c N log^10 N / tau0^b for tau0^a <= N <= N1 < N2 <= min(2N, tau0^(a(1+2 delta))), then zeta has no zero on sigma >= 1 - (b/a)(1 - 2 delta), t = tau0, for tau0 > c(delta).
claims.assessment: Statement and proof read as page images from a supplied scan; not audited. By the author's statement the Lindelof hypothesis is used at one point only, to bound by delta^3 log tau0 the zeros in a fixed box to the right of the line to which Turan's second main theorem is applied; the kernel lemma and a passage repeated from an earlier section were not read.
claims.rationale: The published best form of the implication from prime sums at one height to the absence of zeros at that height; this notebook's conditional exclusions for zeta rediscover its method with a count as the hypothesis, weaker in the lengths needed; neither statement implies the other.
claims.next_action: Read the rest of the section for anything that replaces the count.
claims.formalization_scope: Not formalized; no Lean work assigned.
